My orchard has mango trees that flower early, can I put my hives there and how oftten must I open them?

Place the beehives among the mango trees where nectar is available, under light shade and shielded from wind and rain. Set them on four tar-coated pillars. Apply citronella inside each hive to attract swarms. Once the colony is established, make the first opening roughly eight days later and repeat the visit every eight days, always in full gear with a lit smoker. Harvest only the capped frames at night or very early in the morning. An experienced beekeeper or ITRA/ICAT Sotouboua can advise on the right hive type and disease control.
My farm has a strip of wildflowers along the fence, is that a good place for my hives and what rooutine should I follow?

The beehives should be positioned in the strip of wildflowers where nectar is present, under light shade and protected from wind and rain. Place each hive on four pillars that are coated with tar. Rub the interior of each hive with citronella to lure swarms. After the colony settles, open the first hive about eight days later and continue visiting every eight days, always wearing full gear and using a lit smoker. Harvest only capped frames at night or very early morning. An experienced beekeeper or ITRA/ICAT Sotouboua can help you choose the proper hive and check for disease.
I have a tiny ccao garden on the Plateaux Ouest and I want to know how to put shade in place before planting in July.

You must first check that your garden gets between 1,200 and 2,000 mm of rain each year, that the soil is rich, deep and well-drained at least 80-100 cm, and that you own the land for the long term. Plant the cacao seedlings in June-July as the season advises. Right after planting, establish a provisional shade using banana plants around the young cacao. Then set up a permanent agroforestry shade grid with trees spaced 12 m by 10 m, which equals about 90 trees per hectare; on a 0.25 ha plot that is roughly 22 shade trees. Each month protect the tops of the cacao trees from psyllids and caterpillars and the bases from termites, and cut a firebreak before the dry season. For planting material and shade design, go to ICAT or ITRA.
I just got cassava cuttings, how deep shoudl I put them and which way shoould they face?

You must bury two-thirds of each cassava cutting, laying it slanted with the node-tops pointing up; do not lay the cutting flat. First cut healthy stems that are six to twelve months old into pieces 15 to 25 cm long with at least five nodes and plant them within three days. Dig holes spaced one metre by one metre, which yields about ten thousand plants per hectare. If you are planting together with maize, wait two weeks after the maize is in the ground before you place the cassava cuttings. Weed the plot two to three times while the plants are still small. For clean improved cuttings, especially if mosaic has been a problem, see ITRA or a registered producer.
My neighbour says cowpeea needs a special seed, what should I use for my field?

Use a resistant improved cowpea variety that matures in 55-75 days. Plant it after the rains start, between mid-June and early July. If you opt for an extra-early variety, keep rows 60-65 cm apart and pockets 40 cm apart; for an intermediate variety, keep rows 80 cm apart and pockets 40 cm apart, placing three seeds per pocket. Weed the field about two weeks after sowing. Then use the three flowering-stage sprays for pod protection. To get a variety that matches your grain or fodder goal, go to ICAT.
I have a medium-size plot and want to grow coowpea for fodder, what spacing do I need and what comes next?

For cowpea grown for fodder, if you select an intermediate-maturity type, plant the rows 80 cm apart and keep seed pockets 40 cm apart, putting three grains per pocket. Start with a resistant improved 55-75 day cowpea variety that meets your grain or fodder aim. Sow your seed in the period from mid-June to early July while the rains are strong. Two weeks after sowing do the first weeding of the field. Then follow the three flowering-stage sprays to protect the pods. To obtain a variety matched to your goal, consult ICAT.
what row and pocket distances should i use for cowpea if i want to plant extra-early seeds in my garden

When planting extra-early cowpea (60-65 days) set the rows 60-65 cm apart and the seed pockets 40 cm apart, placing three grains in each pocket. Use a resistant improved 55-75 day cowpea variety that fits your grain or fodder purpose. Sow the seeds in mid-June to early July during the strong rainy period. About two weeks after sowing perform the first weeding. Later apply the three flowering-stage sprays to protect the pods. For a variety that matches your aim, see ICAT.
can you tell me the exact time to do the first cowpea weeding and the later sprays

The first weeding of cowpea should be carried out about ~2 weeks after sowing the seeds. Following that, you must make three sprays during the flowering stage to protect the cowpea pods. Plant a resistant improved variety that reaches maturity in 55-75 days. Arrange rows based on the variety: extra-early at 60-65 cm between rows, 40 cm between pockets, or intermediate at 80 cm between rows, keeping pockets 40 cm apart and three grains per pocket. sow your cowpea between mid-June and early July when rains are strong. For a variety matched to your grain or fodder aim, consult ICAT.
i heard i must weed cowpea twice is the first weeding ~2 weeks after sowing and then spray

The first weeding of cowpea is done about ~2 weeks after sowing the seeds. Then you must apply three sprays during the flowering stage to keep the cowpea pods safe. Plant a resistant improved cowpea variety that matures in 55-75 days. Use row spacing according to the type: extra-early 60-65 cm between rows, 40 cm between pockets, or intermediate 80 cm between rows, same pocket spacing, with three seeds per pocket. sow the cowpea between mid-June and early July when the rains are strong. For a variety that fits your grain or fodder aim, contact ICAT.
I have a sack of frresh cowpea graiin. How can I keep it safe with ash?

You keep cowpea grain safe by using the ash method and sealing the container. First, sort the grain and make sure it is completely dry because any moisture will cause mould. Place the dry cowpea grain in a clean canari or metal tin. Add sifted ash or fine sand in a volume equal to the grain and stir until the ash is evenly distributed through the cowpea grain. Then spread a layer of ash that is exactly 3 cm thick on top of the mixture. Finally close the canari or tin tightly so no air can enter. If you need information about the approved storage product, consult ICAT.
My cowpea beans are still a little wet aftre drying. How can I keep them safe from bugs until I sell them?

Treat the cowpea grain with an approved storage insecticide like an Actellic type at the label dose. First you must sort the beans and dry them fully, because any moisture will cause mould and ruin the crop. After the grain is completely dry, apply the insecticide exactly as the label tells you. Then you may use the ash or sand technique: stir an equal amount of sifted ash or fine sand through the grain in a tin, add a 3 cm layer of ash on top and seal the container. Or you can follow the oil method: add 15-30 ml of groundnut, palm or neem oil for each 2.5 kg of grain, mix well and close the lid. For the current approved product, contact ICAT.
maman i just finished the millet harvest how should i keep the leftovers for my goats during the dry months

You should collect the cereal straw, the legume haulm from cowpea or groundnut, and the dried tuber peelings right after harvest and place them on raised racks in a dry spot. Then treat the dry cereal straw with urea: dissolve about 2.5 kg of urea in 25 L of water, spread the mixture over each 100 kg of straw, layer it and pack it into a lined pit. Cover the pit and let it cure, wearing gloves and boots for safety. After curing, open the pit and give the treated straw to the goats. Also sprinkle salt water on any cobs or stover you offer and be sure the animals have clean water and a mineral source. For a safe demonstration of the urea-treatment pit, visit the ICAT.
My goats eat a lot of straw but it seems not enough in the dry saeson. What should I do with the harvest leftovers?

Immediately after harvest you should gather the cereal straw, the legume haulm from cowpea or groundnut, and the dried tuber peelings and store them on raised racks in a dry place. Then treat the dry cereal straw with urea by mixing about 2.5 kg of urea with 25 L of water for each 100 kg of straw, layering the mixture and packing it into a lined pit. Cover the pit, allow it to cure while wearing gloves and boots, and later open it to feed the treated straw to your goats. Sprinkle salt water on any cobs or stover you also give and always provide clean water and a mineral source. For a safe demonstration of the urea-treatment pit, see the ICAT.
During the dry season my goats and ewe have only old stalks left. How can I improve their feed?

Collect all the cereal straw, legume haulm such as cowpea or groundnut, and dried tuber peelings and keep them on raised racks in a dry environment. Prepare a urea solution of about 2.5 kg urea in 25 L water for each 100 kg of straw, spread it over the straw, pack it tightly in a lined pit, cover it and let it cure while wearing gloves and boots, then open the pit. Once the treated straw is ready, sprinkle salt water on the cobs or stover you will give to your goats and sheep. Provide clean water and a mineral source together with the feed. For assistance with the urea-treatment pit, go to ICAT.
i just pulled up my groundnut plants how can i keep the nitrogen they added to my field

Cut the groundnut stems right at the soil surface so the nodules stay in the ground. After that, sow a cereal crop in the same plot to capture the nitrogen from the groundnut. Make sure the field is on light, well-drained soil as you plant the cereal. This follows the rule to rotate groundnut with cereals and not to grow groundnut on the same land two years running. If rosette or leaf spot troubles you each year, go to ICAT for a tolerant groundnut variety before you start the next cycle.
My groundnut harvest is done, what do I do next to use the nitrogeen left behind?

First, cut the groundnut stems at ground level, leaving the nitrogen-fixing nodules in the soil. Then plant a cereal in that same field to absorb the nitrogen from the groundnut. Ensure the soil is light and drains well when you sow the cereal. This respects the rotation advice that groundnut should not be planted on the same land for two consecutive seasons. If you repeatedly see rosette or leaf spot, seek a tolerant groundnut variety from ICAT before planting again.
what's the right thing to do with my groundnut field after harvest to keep the nitrogen benefit

Cut the groundnut stems at ground level, leaving the nitrogen-fixing nodules in the soil. Then sow a cereal crop in the same field to take up the nitrogen from the groundnut. Make sure the soil you sow into is light and well-drained. This respects the rotation rule that groundnut should not be grown on the same land for two consecutive years. If you have yearly problems with rosette or leaf spot, visit ICAT to obtain a tolerant groundnut variety before you plant again.
my guinea fowl keets seem weak in the morning what feeding routine should i follow

Feed your guinea fowl keets small quantities of starter feed several times a day, placing it in low feeders they can easily access. Use a fine protein-rich starter for each feeding and keep the water always clean, refilling it often. Keep the brooder clean, dry and sheltered from wind and rain, with the mother-hen present. Check the litter both morning and evening, keep it dry and disinfected, and isolate any keet that looks weak. Maintain this routine of frequent, little feedings and clean water. If the guinea fowl keets keep dying or develop discharge or diarrhoea, consult a livestock auxiliary.
do i need to give my guinea fowl keets big meals once or feed them a little all day

Give your guinea fowl keets little portions of feed several times each day, using low feeders that are easy for them to use. Offer a fine protein-rich starter at every feeding and keep the water always clean, changing it regularly. Ensure the brooder is clean, dry and protected from wind and rain, and let the mother-hen stay with the keets. Check the litter in the morning and evening, keep it dry and disinfected, and shut in any keet that appears weak. Continue this schedule of frequent small feedings and clean water. If the guinea fowl keets keep dying or show discharge or diarrhoea, a livestock auxiliary can help.
My neighbour says I should give my three-month-old keets a big bowl of feed once a day. I only have a small wooden brooder with the mother-poultry. How often should I feed and water them?

You should offer the keets small portions of feed and water many times throughout the day, using low trays they can reach easily. Provide a fine protein-rich starter at each feeding. Change the water frequently so it stays clean. Keep the mother-hen with the keets inside a clean, dry brooder that protects them from wind and rain and keep them apart from adult birds. Make sure the bedding stays dry and disinfected, inspecting it each morning and evening, and isolate any keet that appears weak. If the keets continue to die or show any discharge or diarrhoea, go to a livestock auxiliary.
Is there any extra fertiliser needed for corn in the Plateaux region?

In the Plateaux region the maize fertiliser programme uses only the standard doses, with no extra regional complement. First, after sowing, place four bags of NPK 15-15-15 (200 kg per hectare) in a pocket 5-10 cm from each seedling, waiting 10-15 days and ensuring the bag does not touch the plant. Then, at panicle initiation about 30-45 days after sowing, apply urea as a top-dress at 100 kg per hectare. No additional potash or phosphate is added for Plateaux. Finally, have ICAT verify the plan for any soil-specific adjustment.
My corn started to show the first tassels, what fertilizer should I add now?

At the tasseling stage you must apply the top-dress urea for maize. First, remember you already put the base NPK 15-15-15 at 200 kg per hectare in a pocket 5-10 cm from the seedlings 10-15 days after sowing, keeping it away from the plant. Then, when the crop is at panicle initiation, which is 30-45 days after sowing, spread urea at a rate of 100 kg per hectare over the whole field. If you need a soil-specific dose, go to ICAT for advice.
My feld is ready but the rain just started, what spacing and depth do I need for my maize seds?

Lay your maize rows 80 cm apart and set pockets in the rows. Use pocket spacing of 35 cm for varieties under 90 days, 40 cm for 90-100 days, and 50 cm for over 100 days. Put 2-3 seeds in each pocket at a depth of 3-5 cm. Seed with 20-25 kg per hectare of treated improved seed. Do not sow until the rains are steady and not after a single shower. Perform the first weeding 10-15 days after sowing and thin any three-seedling spots to two plants. For an improved variety that matches your region and season, consult ICAT.
i planted maize after the rains came when is the right time to weed and how many seedlings should stay in each row pocket

Carry out the first weeding 10-15 days after sowing the maize, then thin the seedlings so that only 2 plants stay where 3 have emerged. Apply 20-25 kg per hectare of treated improved seed, laying rows 80 cm apart. Place seeds in in-row pockets spaced 35 cm for varieties under 90 days, 40 cm for 90-100 days, or 50 cm for longer cycles, with 2-3 seeds per pocket at a depth of 3-5 cm. Avoid a false start by not sowing on a first isolated shower; wait for reliable rains. Sow when rains are established, for example April-May in Maritime/Plateaux or June-July in Centrale/Kara/Savanes. To get a suitable improved variety for your area, see ICAT.
i just threshed my maize and the kernels feel a bit soft how must i get them ready for the store

You need to dry the maize grain hard until it reaches about 13-14% moisture, so the kernels snap instead of denting, before you store it. First, sweep out your storage building and take away any residues from the previous season because the larger grain borer can survive there. Next, put the dried maize grain into sturdy, sealed bags or bins that are in good condition. After that, blend an approved grain protectant or dried neem-leaf powder evenly through the maize grain. Do all these actions right after harvest. If the maize grain still shows insects, go to ICAT for the currently approved storage insecticide.
Is it enough to just sweep the floor of my granary before storing corn?

No, you need to clean the whole store and eliminate every piece of last-season residue where the larger grain borer may survive. Next, dry the maize to roughly 13-14% moisture so the kernels snap rather than dent. Then place the dry grain in sturdy, sealed bags or bins. Add an approved grain protectant or dried neem-leaf powder and mix it evenly through the grain. Should insects remain, contact ICAT for the currently approved storage insecticide.
my maize store still has old stalks from last year can i just put the new grain in

You must first clean the store and take away all residues from the previous season because the larger grain borer lives in them. Then dry the maize until it reaches about 13-14% moisture so it snaps rather than dents. After that, put the dried maize in sound, sealed bags or bins and mix an approved grain protectant or dried neem-leaf powder through the grain. If insects are still present, go to ICAT for the currently approved storage insecticide.
The store still has old grain, I just harvested mazie. What do I do beefore putting it away?

Dry the newly harvested maize until it reaches a hard texture with about 13-14% moisture, so it snaps instead of dents. Then clean the storage building and take out any leftover grain from the last season because larger grain borer can survive in those remnants. After cleaning, put the dried maize into sturdy, sealed bags or bins. Thoroughly mix an approved grain protectant or dried neem-leaf powder into the grain before you seal the bags or bins. If infestation continues, see ICAT for the currently approved storage insecticide.
I have some brewery grain and fish meal, what else do I need for a proper boar feed?

A proper pig feed must contain three groups of ingredients. Combine energy sources such as maize, sorghum, cassava or yam and their peelings, brans and brewery grains with the protein sources you already have, like fish meal, adding soybean, groundnut cake and a little cottonseed or palm-kernel cake if you wish. Finish the mix with minerals and salt. Offer clean water at all times and let the pigs drink whenever they like. Boil any restaurant scraps before you add them to the feed to avoid disease. Increase the feed amount as the pigs grow. Give iron to piglets in the first days of life. For a costed ration and piglet iron or deworming details, consult a veterinary or extension officer.
Do I have to give my swine water all the time or can I limit it?

Pigs must have access to clean water whenever they want, so keep a trough filled with fresh water at all times. The water should be clean and refreshed regularly so the pigs can drink freely. Before adding any restaurant leftovers to the feed, boil them to prevent disease. Prepare the ration using three groups: energy items such as maize, sorghum, cassava or yam peelings, brans and brewery grains; protein items like soybean, groundnut cake, fish or blood meal, with only a little cottonseed or palm-kernel cake; and a mix of minerals and salt. Increase the amount of feed as each pig gets bigger, and give iron to piglets during their first days. For a detailed, costed ration and piglet iron or deworming advice, see the veterinary or extension officer.
my sow just gave birth and the piglets are newborns while the older pigs are getting larger how do i manage their feed

Give iron to the newborn piglets in the first days and raise the feed amount as the older pigs grow. First, create a balanced ration from three sections: energy items such as maize, sorghum, cassava or yam together with peelings, brans and brewery grains; protein sources like soybean, groundnut cake, fish or blood meal, and a modest inclusion of cottonseed or palm-kernel cake; then add minerals and salt. Ensure clean water is always freely available. Boil any restaurant scraps before they are added to the feed to avoid disease. Provide the piglets with an iron supplement during their initial days. For a cost-estimated ration or the specific iron amount, consult a veterinary or extension officer.
What are the basic parts of a swine pen to keep them healthy and tidy?

Your pig pen should have a wall about ~1.2 m high, an exercise zone and a footbath at the entrance. First, create at least four distinct compartments for the boar, the sows, a nursing sow and the weaned pigs so disease spread is limited. Use banco for local varieties or cement bricks for improved breeds when building the walls. Place the whole structure on a rammed or cemented floor that can be cleaned and disinfected. Add the footbath at the gate and make sure the pigs never foul the pen without supervision. Lastly, get an extension officer to measure the pens to fit the number of animals you own.
what should i include in my pig pen to keep them from making a mess and staying healthy

The pen needs a wall of roughly ~1.2 m, an exercise area and a footbath at the entrance. Begin by setting up at least four compartments for a boar, the sows, a nursing sow and the weaned piglets so that breeding and health are managed. Build the walls with banco for local pigs or cement bricks for improved breeds. Lay a rammed or cemented floor that you can clean and disinfect. Add the footbath at the gate and ensure the pigs never foul the pen without supervision. End by seeing an extension officer who will adjust the pen size to suit your herd.
I want to set up a new pig shelter. How tall shoulld the wall be and what must I add at the gate?

The wall of your pig shelter should be about 1.2 m high and you must place a footbath right at the entrance. First, split the enclosure into at least four separate sections for boars, sows, a nursing sow and weaned piglets so you can control breeding and health. Then build the structures with banco if you keep local breeds or with cement bricks for improved breeds, always on a compacted rammed or cemented floor that you can wash and disinfect. Include an exercise area inside the pen for the pigs to move around. Make sure the animals never soil the pen without supervision. Finally, ask an extension officer to size the pens according to the number of pigs you have.
My coop has a few grown chickens and a batch of new chiicks, how oftten must I feed each group?

Feed the new chicks about three times per day and the grown chickens about two times per day after you crush and mix the feed. Start by preparing a daily ration that blends energy sources such as maize, sorghum, millet or brans, protein sources like cowpea, soy, oil cakes, fish meal, termites or maggots, and minerals and vitamins from bone or shell powder together with a supplement. Serve the mixed feed to the chicks in three feedings and to the adult chickens in two feedings. Ensure clean water is always present because a shortage hits hens fast. For specific ration amounts for your flock, contact ICAT.
the straw in my poultry house is getting wet and smelly how do i manage the litter

Daily sweeping of the floor will remove wet droppings. Replace the entire straw or rice husk litter every 2-3 months. When you change the litter, first disinfect the floor with an appropriate disinfectant. After disinfection, spread fresh straw or rice husks as new bedding. Keep the building as an improved traditional poultry house with at least two rooms, separating adults from chicks, and supply enough feeders, waterers, perches and nest boxes. The first health priority is vaccination against Newcastle. You can seek further support from ICAT about an improving rooster and vaccination.
Birs are dying in my yard all together, what is the first step?

Administer the Newcastle disease vaccine to every chicken because the disease can cause sudden, collective deaths. Next, build an Improved Traditional Poultry House of banco or straw, roughly three by three metres, with two rooms, adult and chick sections, situated near your house. Sweep the coop daily and replace the straw or rice-husk litter every two to three months, disinfecting each replacement. Ensure you have sufficient feeders, waterers, perches and nest boxes so the chickens do not fight over them. For the vaccine and advice on an improving rooster, contact ICAT.
How much fertilizer and at what stages should I apply it for my half-heectare lowland rice after transplanting?

The plan is to apply NPK 15-15-15 at 200 kg per hectare about one week after transplanting, which equals 100 kg for your 0.5 ha area. Then use urea at 100 kg per hectare, split into two equal applications of 50 kg each, first at the tillering stage and second at panicle initiation. First, raise seedlings for about twenty-one days in a nursery. Next, transplant two to three plants per pocket with 20 x 20 cm spacing. After the seven-day interval, spread the NPK blend across the field. When the crop reaches tillering, apply the first urea split, and repeat the same amount at panicle initiation. For variety matching and rate advice, go to ICAT.
I have a 0.25 ha rainfed paddy plot, what are the exact NPK and urea amounts I need?

For rainfed rice you need 150 kg ha⁻¹ NPK, which is 37.5 kg on a quarter-hectare, and urea at 50 kg ha⁻¹ split, giving 12.5 kg for your field. Start by raising seedlings for roughly 21 days, then transplant 2-3 plants per 20 x 20 cm pocket. After transplant, apply the 37.5 kg NPK and the split urea dose of 12.5 kg. Weed the rice at 15-25 days and again at about 40 days. Protect the crop from birds from flowering to harvest. For variety selection and rate confirmation, go to ICAT.
What amout of NPK and urea should I put on my rainefd rice field that is 0.25 ha?

For rainfed rice you should apply 150 kg ha⁻¹ NPK, which is 37.5 kg on a quarter-hectare, and urea at 50 kg ha⁻¹ split, giving 12.5 kg for your plot. Begin by raising seedlings for about 21 days, then transplant 2-3 plants per pocket spaced 20 x 20 cm. After transplant, distribute the 37.5 kg NPK and the split urea dose of 12.5 kg. Weed the rice at 15-25 days and again around 40 days. Keep birds away from flowering to harvest. For variety matching and exact rate advice, visit ICAT.
i planted sorghum seeds on the ridges after the rain but now the pockets are crowded what must i do

You need to thin the sorghum to two to three plants per pocket when the seedlings are two to three weeks old. First, remember you sowed on ridges after a heavy rain, putting three to five grains per pocket at a depth of three to five centimetres and using six to eight kilograms of treated seed per hectare. At the two to three week stage count the seedlings and pull out the extras until only two to three remain in each pocket. Then wait for the first weeding, being careful not to break the ridges, and apply NPK fertilizer at 150 to 200 kilograms per hectare followed by urea at 50 to 100 kilograms per hectare. Keep the soil pressed up against lodging and contact ICAT to align the sorghum variety with your local rains.
My srghum seedlings look too many in each hole after a few weks, how should I handle it?

Thin the sorghum seedlings to two to three plants per pocket at the age of two to three weeks. You had earlier sowed on ridges after a strong rain, placing three to five seeds per pocket at three to five centimetres depth and using six to eight kilograms of treated seed per hectare. When the two to three week point arrives, examine each pocket and remove the surplus seedlings so only two to three stay. After thinning perform the first weeding without disturbing the ridges, then spread NPK at 150 to 200 kilograms per hectare and later add urea at 50 to 100 kilograms per hectare. Push the earth up to prevent lodging and seek advice from ICAT for matching the sorghum cycle to your prefecture's rains.
After sowing sorghhum on ridges, I ntoice too many plants in the pockets after a couple of weeks. What do I need to do?

You must thin the sorghum to two to three plants per pocket at two to three weeks after sowing. First, you placed three to five seeds per pocket on ridges after a heavy rain, at three to five centimetres depth, using six to eight kilograms of treated seed per hectare. When the seedlings reach two to three weeks, inspect each pocket and pull out the surplus until only two to three plants stay. Then perform the first weeding, taking care not to break the ridges, and apply NPK at 150 to 200 kilograms per hectare, followed by urea at 50 to 100 kilograms per hectare. Keep the soil mounded up to avoid lodging and approach ICAT for guidance on matching the sorghum variety to your prefecture's rains.
My sorghum field has many seedlings per pocket after the frst weeks, how should I thin them and what follows?

Thin the sorghum to two to three plants per pocket at the two to three week stage. You originally sowed on ridges after a heavy rain, putting three to five grains per pocket at a depth of three to five centimetres and using six to eight kilograms of treated seed per hectare. At two to three weeks count the seedlings and remove the extras so only two to three remain in each pocket. After thinning, carry out the first weeding without breaking the ridges, then spread NPK fertilizer at 150 to 200 kilograms per hectare and later apply urea at 50 to 100 kilograms per hectare. Push the earth up to keep lodging away and get in touch with ICAT to match a sorghum variety's cycle to your local rains.
The soil is still wet and I see some weeds, should I wait before weeding my soy seedlinngs?

Buy certified soybean seed treated for damping-off from the ICAT/Sotouboua seed farm and sow it right away. Two weeks after sowing, go into the nursery and pull out any weeds that have emerged, regardless of soil moisture. Then, three weeks after the sowing date, return to the nursery and repeat the weeding to keep the area weed-free. This schedule stops the fungi that make soybean seedlings topple at the soil surface. The source for the treated seed is ICAT/Sotouboua seed farm.
The soil is still wet from last night's rain and I have soya seed ready. Is it safe to sow now?

Buy certified soybean seed that has been treated against damping-off and sow it even if the soil is moist. After two weeks, go into the nursery and pull any weeds that have sprouted, keeping the beds tidy. After three weeks from sowing, repeat the weeding to maintain a clean environment. Following these steps prevents the damping-off fungus that causes soybean seedlings to topple at the soil line. You can obtain the certified seed from the ICAT/Sotouboua seed farm.
Is it okay to pull up the soy pants afer they're ripe?

No, you need to cut the soybean stems at ground level and leave the nitrogen-fixing root nodules in the soil. Before this you would have sown certified seed that was treated against damping-off and weeded at two weeks and again three weeks after emergence. You must not grow soy on the same plot for more than two years in a row, which helps keep parasite pressure low. Then you should plant a cereal crop to take advantage of the nitrogen left by the soybean nodules. For certified seed advice, see the ICAT/Sotouboua seed farm.
Why is it important to grow a grain after my soya?

Growing a grain after soybean lets the grain absorb the nitrogen that soybean adds to the soil. Begin by sowing certified soybean seed treated against damping-off, and weed the field at two weeks and again three weeks later. When you harvest, cut the soybean stems at ground level and leave the nitrogen-fixing root nodules in the ground. Then plant a cereal in the same plot so the cereal benefits from the nitrogen left by the soy. Remember not to grow soybean on the same plot for more than two years in a row to reduce parasite pressure. For seed, see ICAT/Sotouboua seed farm.
should i tie my yam vines now and when must i pull the first weeds

Tie the yam vines right after you plant them and carry out the first weeding at the proper time. First, pick a deep, rested soil that has no stones and has been left fallow for at least five years, or use a short Mucuna fallow if you have little land. Next, shape mounds that are between 40 and 80 cm high; on good soil place them about 1.4 by 1.4 m apart, giving roughly 5,000 mounds per hectare, while on poorer soil use 1 by 1.5 m spacing for about 6,500 mounds per hectare. Then plant healthy seed setts whose cut surfaces have healed in shade and are dusted with wood ash. For a good-storage variety, visit ICAT or ITRA.
Do I need to secure yam vines now and when shold the first weeding happen?

Secure the yam vines immediately after planting and carry out the first weeding at the appropriate time. Start by selecting deep, rested, stone-free soil that has been left fallow for five years or more, or use a brief Mucuna fallow if the land is scarce. Build mounds 40-80 cm tall, placing them 1.4 x 1.4 m apart on fertile ground (about 5,000 mounds per hectare) or 1 x 1.5 m on poorer ground (about 6,500 mounds per hectare). Use healthy seed setts, let the cut faces heal in shade and dust them with wood ash before planting. For a good-storage variety, go to ICAT or ITRA.
i just planted my yam setts when must i tie the vines and when should i pull the first weeds

Tie the yam vines right after you plant the setts and carry out the first weeding at the proper time. First, pick a deep, rested, stone-free field that has been left fallow for at least five years or, if you have little land, use a short Mucuna fallow. Then shape mounds that are between 40 and 80 cm high, arranging them at about 1.4 x 1.4 m on fertile soil (roughly 5,000 mounds per hectare) or at 1 x 1.5 m on poorer soil (about 6,500 mounds per hectare). Use healthy yam seed setts, let the cut faces heal in shade and dust them with wood ash before planting. For a good-storage variety such as TDr 747 or Florido, go to ICAT or ITRA.
during the rainy season my cassava leaves are getting angular brown spots and the new leaves are wilting what steps must i take

Those symptoms indicate cassava bacterial blight, which is caused by the bacterium Xanthomonas axonopodis pv. manihotis. First, walk the plot and pull out any plant that displays angular water-soaked spots, wilting young leaves, shoot die-back, or gum on the stem, and destroy those plants. After each removal, disinfect your pruning tools before moving to the next plant. Next, take cuttings only from plants that show no symptoms and use them for replanting. Plant a resistant cassava variety and rotate the plot to a new location. For clean resistant cuttings you may contact ITRA or a registered producer, and you can ask ICAT to verify the diagnosis.
The leaves of my manioc are showing angular water-soaked spots and the shoots are dying, can I still use those stems for my next planting?

No, you must not use those stems for planting because they carry cassava bacterial blight. First, select cuttings only from plants that show no angular spots, no wilting leaves and no gum on the stems. Then cut those healthy stems and discard any that display the symptoms. After each cutting, disinfect your tools before moving to the next plant to avoid moving the bacterium. Destroy any affected plants immediately to stop further spread. Finally, obtain clean resistant cuttings from ITRA or a registered producer and, if needed, ask ICAT to confirm the disease.
maman i heard there is a big disease hurting cassava here which one is it

Cassava mosaic disease is the most common and damaging cassava disease in Togo. First, pull out and destroy any plants that show strong yellow mottling, pale leaves, or twisted, puckered foliage. Then, for the next sowing, cut only from plants that have normal green leaves and no deformation. Avoid taking cuttings from any mottled or deformed stem. Plant an improved tolerant variety obtained from ITRA or a registered cutting producer and keep the stand uniform and well fed. If you see angular water-soaked spots with wilting instead of leaf deformation, go to ICAT for confirmation; for clean tolerant cuttings, contact ITRA.
My manioc field is losing a lot of its yield, could it be cassava mosaic disease? How much can it cost me?

Cassava mosaic disease can cause losses ranging from 15-95% of your harvest. Remove and destroy any plants that are strongly mottled or stunted. When you replant, select cuttings only from plants that look healthy and avoid any mottled or deformed stems. Choose an improved tolerant variety supplied by ITRA or a registered cutting producer and maintain a uniform, well-fed stand. For clean tolerant cuttings, contact ITRA.
my neighbor says using only resistant cassava will stop the mosaic is that true

Using a combination of resistant or tolerant cassava varieties together with susceptible ones lowers the incidence of cassava mosaic disease. Begin by purchasing improved tolerant cuttings from ITRA or an authorized cutting supplier. Plant those tolerant cuttings side by side with the susceptible varieties you normally use. Maintain a uniform, well-fed stand to support plant vigor. If any plant shows strong yellow mottling, leaf twisting or shrinkage, uproot and destroy it because sprays do not work. For the following planting, take cuttings solely from plants that appear healthy and never from mottled stems. For clean tolerant cuttings, see ITRA.
is it useful to grow tolerant cassava together with my usual ones to fight the mosaic virus

Growing tolerant cassava together with your usual susceptible varieties reduces the incidence of cassava mosaic disease. Start by obtaining improved tolerant cuttings from ITRA or a certified cutting producer. Then mix those tolerant cuttings with the susceptible cuttings when you plant. Ensure the stand remains uniform and well-fed to keep the plants vigorous. As soon as you notice plants with strong yellow mottling, leaf twisting or shrinkage, uproot and destroy them because no spray can cure the infection. For the next crop, take cuttings only from plants that look healthy and never from mottled or deformed stems. For clean tolerant cuttings, go to ITRA.
the cassava i planted is not growing tall and the leaves are pale and twisted is this a disease

Yes, pale and twisted leaves with very short cassava plants are signs of cassava mosaic disease causing stunting. Pull up and destroy the strongly mottled, stunted cassava plants now. For the next crop, take cuttings only from cassava plants that appear healthy, avoiding any mottled or deformed stems. Use improved tolerant cassava cuttings from ITRA or a registered cutting producer and maintain a uniform, well-fed stand. ITRA can provide the clean tolerant cuttings you need.
my field got a lot of twisted cassava leaves after i used cuttings from the previous harvest what went wrong

The problem is that cassava mosaic disease is introduced when cuttings are taken from already-infected cassava stems and replanted. First, uproot and destroy the strongly mottled, stunted cassava plants because they will not recover and they keep feeding the whitefly that spreads the disease. Then, when you plant again, take cuttings only from cassava plants that appear healthy, with even green foliage and normal shape. After that, plant an improved tolerant cassava variety sourced from ITRA or a registered cutting producer and keep a uniform, well-fed stand. For clean tolerant cuttings, see ITRA.
my cassava leaves are in patches of yellow mottling is that from insects

Yes, whiteflies moving between plants spread the African cassava mosaic virus, creating the patchy yellow mottling you observe. Remove and destroy the strongly mottled, stunted cassava plants in those patches immediately. For the next planting, cut only from plants that have normal green leaves and no signs of deformation. Obtain improved tolerant cuttings from ITRA or a registered cutting producer and plant them, maintaining a uniform, well-fed stand. If you need clean tolerant cuttings, ITRA can provide them.
my cows keep getting thinner and look pale could it be from the flies near the river

What you are describing is nagana in your cattle caused by tsetse fly bites. First, go to the veterinary service so they can confirm the disease and supply the proper trypanocide, and do not try to choose a drug yourself. Then make sure the cattle have abundant good feed and clean water to help them fight the illness. After that, keep them away from riverine bush during the biting hours and look into fly-control options to lower fly exposure. You need to see the veterinary service for a professional diagnosis and correct treatment.
The herd is losing weigt fast and their gums are white, is this the tsetse problem?

Those signs indicate nagana in your cattle resulting from tsetse fly bites. Contact the veterinary service right away for a diagnosis and the right trypanocide, and avoid guessing any medication. Next, provide plenty of nutritious feed and fresh water so the cattle can stay strong while sick. Then prevent fly contact by not grazing in riverine bush during the biting periods and consider measures to control the flies. You should see the veterinary service for accurate diagnosis and appropriate medication.
my oxen are getting thinner their coats are rough and their gums look pale what can i do

Those signs indicate trypanosomiasis (nagana) in your cattle. First stop letting the cattle graze in riverine bush where tsetse flies bite, especially during the biting hours. Then look into fly-control measures to lower the number of bites. Make sure the cattle receive enough good feed and clean water so they can stay strong. After these actions you must bring the cattle to the veterinary service for a proper diagnosis and the correct trypanocide. Only the veterinary service can supply the right treatment.
My heifer looks thin, his coat is rough and his gums are white. What should I do?

The thin bull with a rough coat and pale gums is showing signs of nagana. Give the bull plenty of good feed each day and ensure clean water is always available so he can stay strong. Keep the bull away from riverine bush during the times when tsetse flies bite. If possible, use any fly-control method you have to lower the number of flies. When these signs appear, go to the veterinary service for a proper diagnosis and the correct trypanocide. Do not try to guess a drug or dose on your own. The veterinary service will confirm the disease and provide the right treatment.
My cowpea field keeps losing flowes and the pods have holes, what is happening and how can I stop it?

The loss of flowers and holes in pods are caused by flower thrips, pod borers and aphids on your cowpea. First, sow a resistant improved cowpea variety that matures in 55 to 75 days when the rains are strong, usually from mid-June to early July. About two weeks after sowing, do the first weeding to keep the field tidy. When flower buds appear at 30 to 35 days after sowing, spray an approved insecticide at the labelled rate. Ten days later apply the second spray, and repeat another ten days after that for the third spray. These three applications are needed because the insects re-invade in waves. For the current approved product and exact dose, visit ICAT.

My groundnut leaves are turning yellow and I see dark round spots, and the plants are shedding leaves fasster than usual. What can I do?

Those signs are groundnut leaf spot caused by Cercospora fungi. First, avoid planting groundnut on the same plot in consecutive years and rotate with a cereal crop. Next, select and sow a groundnut variety that tolerates leaf spot. Then, after you finish harvesting, clear or bury any remaining groundnut residues to eliminate the fungus source. Also, make sure to harvest your groundnut crop at the proper time so weakened plants do not drop pods early. For advice on resistant varieties and whether a fungicide is needed, contact ICAT.
my groundnut plants are shedding leaves quickly and the pods look small what is happening

When groundnut leaves fall early, the plants cannot supply enough material to develop pods, which lowers the harvest. Do not repeat groundnut on the same field year after year; rotate with cereal crops. Plant a tolerant groundnut type and clear or bury previous groundnut residues. Pick the crop when it is mature, as a weakened plant will drop its pods. For advice on resistant varieties or whether a fungicide is needed, see ICAT.
The leaves of my groundnut are yellowing, dropping early and have dark roud spots. How can I handle this?

You are dealing with groundnut leaf spot, therefore you should rotate your groundnut with cereals and avoid sowing groundnut on the same land year after year. Harvest the crop at the proper time to keep the plants healthy and prevent early pod loss. If you need help selecting a resistant variety or assessing the need for a fungicide, contact ICAT.
groundnut leaves in my garden are showing dark round spots and are falling off early what steps must i take

That is groundnut leaf spot, so do not grow groundnut on the same field consecutively; rotate the field with a cereal crop. Use a tolerant groundnut variety when you plant groundnut again. The leaves of my groundnut are yellowing and dropping eraly, should I change anything in how I manage the field?

Groundnut leaf spot persists in crop residues left behind. Avoid planting groundnut on that land again this year and rotate with a cereal crop. Use a groundnut variety that tolerates the disease. Clear or bury the previous groundnut residues before the new season starts. Make sure to harvest on schedule to prevent early pod loss. If you need help picking a tolerant variety or deciding on a fungicide, visit ICAT.
my peanuts keep getting sick the leaves get dark spots and drop early what should i change

The leaves on my groundnut plants have early yellowing and round spos, and pods are fallign off, what steps should I follow?

These are signs of groundnut leaf spot, so you need to use a tolerant groundnut variety and clear or bury all old groundnut residues. Start by selecting a tolerant groundnut variety, which reduces disease impact. Then clear or bury the previous groundnut trash in the field, as the fungus survives in those residues. Next rotate your groundnut with cereals and do not plant groundnut on the same land in successive years. Also harvest the groundnut on time so the plants stay vigorous and do not drop pods early. For details on resistant varieties and fungicide recommendations, see ICAT.
My field of peanut is full of plants with bunched, distorted leaves and yellow mottling. Is this groundnut rosette?

Yes, those symptoms are caused by groundnut rosette virus complex on groundnut. Remove the badly damaged groundnut plants and destroy them. Afterwards, sow your next groundnut crop early and keep the rows at the close spacing advised. Keep the groundnut plot free of weeds to limit aphid carriers. Finally, obtain a tolerant groundnut variety for the next season. You should see ICAT for resistant seeds.
I found some peanut plants with short, bunched leaves and green mottling. How should I handle this problem?

Those signs point to groundnut rosette, and an early infection will stunt the crop severely. Start by rogueing out and destroying the heavily affected plants you can identify. After that, sow the next groundnut seed early and follow the close spacing recommendation to obtain a dense stand. Keep the plot free of weeds to reduce the aphid hosts that move the virus. For the next cycle, plant a tolerant groundnut variety. To obtain resistant varieties, go to ICAT.
My field is full of weeds and the groundnut leaves look a bit yellow. Will clearring the weeds help with the disease?

Yes, you should keep the groundnut field weed-free to cut down aphid hosts. Plant your groundnut seeds as early as possible and place them at the close spacing that is recommended for the crop. This dense early stand will suffer far less from the virus. When you find plants that are severely affected, pull them out and destroy them right away. For the next season, choose a tolerant groundnut variety. You can obtain resistant varieties by contacting ICAT.
i see my groundnut plants have bunched distorted young leaves with green spots should i treat them

Those symptoms are groundnut rosette and there is no cure, so you must rogue out and destroy the severely affected plants. Then sow early and use the recommended close spacing for the new planting. Keep the field weed-free to limit aphid hosts. Choose a tolerant groundnut variety for the next season. You can obtain resistant varieties from ICAT.
I found my peanut seedlings looking stunted and with distorted leaves, how should I act?

Those symptoms are typical of groundnut rosette, which cannot be treated once present. For the next planting, sow groundnut early and follow the close spacing guideline to achieve a dense canopy. After sowing, remove all weeds from the field to reduce aphid hosts that carry the virus. If you see any severely affected groundnut rosette plants, pull them out and destroy them immediately. Use a tolerant groundnut variety in the next season. Contact ICAT to get resistant varieties.
my sheep s fleece is thinning and they seem to eat less what should i check

The thinning fleece and reduced eating are later and early signs of leucaena poisoning in sheep. Limit leucaena to about a quarter to a third of the ration and never let it dominate the feed. Combine the leucaena with grasses and cereal crop residues to provide enough roughage for the rumen. Introduce any feed adjustment gradually over several days. Provide constant clean water and a mineral or salt source. If the sheep do not start eating again or you notice drooling, a swollen throat, or bloat, consult the veterinary service.
Our heifers are losing hair and seem to have a sore throat after eating a lot of leucaena. Could this be an infection?

This is leucaena poisoning, which is a feeding-related toxicity, not an infectious disease. Cut the leucaena back so it makes up only a quarter to a third of the total ration and never let it dominate the diet. Mix the limited leucaena with grasses and cereal crop residues to provide plenty of roughage for the rumen. Change the feed composition gradually over several days. Ensure the cattle always have clean water and access to a mineral or salt source. If the hair loss and throat swelling do not improve, contact the veterinary service.
My goats have thin wool and are losig appetite afetr I fed them leucaena. How can I fix their diet?

Limit the amount of leucaena for the goats to roughly a quarter to a third of the total ration and do not use it as the principal feed. Trim the leucaena and mix it with grasses and cereal crop residues so the rumen has plenty of roughage. Introduce the new feed mix gradually over several days. Make sure the goats always have clean water and a source of mineral or salt. If appetite does not return or you notice drooling or throat swelling, see the veterinary service.
My lamb are eating a lot of leucaena, can I give them more to grow faster?

Increase of leucaena must be done gradually, spreading the change over several days. Keep leucaena at about a quarter to a third of the total ration and never as the primary feed. Combine the leucaena with grasses and cereal crop residues so the rumen obtains sufficient roughage. Make sure the sheep always have clean water and a mineral or salt source at hand. If you notice continued loss of appetite, drooling, or any sign of bloat, see the veterinary service. I cannot provide an exact timing for the gradual increase.
Rain fell hard last night and now the bottom leaves of my corn are turning pale, no spoots. What's wrong?

The pale, yellow lower leaves on your maize right after a heavy downpour are a sign of nitrogen loss from the root zone. Dig a shallow drainage ditch so the water can run off the plot instead of pooling. When the soil has drained, place a side-dress of urea about 5-10 cm from each stalk, applying roughly 100 kg per hectare at panicle initiation and keep it away from the plant to prevent burning. Continue the second weeding and earthing-up at the scheduled times. ICAT should only be visited if you later notice streaks or dead-heart damage; otherwise no service is needed for this nitrogen loss.
My corn field got heavy rain and now the leaves near the ground are yellowing uniformly, no marks. How should I fix it?

Yellowing of the lower maize leaves after heavy rain is caused by nitrogen loss, not a pest or disease. Begin by opening a shallow drainage channel to let excess water run off the field. After the soil dries, side-dress urea in a pocket 5-10 cm from each maize stem, using about 100 kg/ha at panicle initiation and keep the fertilizer away from the stem so it does not burn. Continue with the second weeding and earthing-up as planned. Should pale streaks on veins or dead-heart appear, consult ICAT.
My field of corn looks fine on top but the leaves at the base are suddenly yellow after the rain, no marks. How can I fix it?

That sudden yellowing of the lower maize leaves after a heavy rain indicates nitrogen loss. Begin by opening a shallow drainage channel to let excess water run off the plot rather than stay. After the water drains, side-dress urea in a pocket positioned 5-10 cm from each stem, applying about 100 kg per hectare at panicle initiation, and keep the fertilizer off the plant so it does not burn. Also keep the second weeding and earthing-up on their planned dates. Should pale streaks appear on leaf veins or you see dead-heart, go to ICAT.
After the rain my corn plants have the lowest leaves turning pale all over, no spots. What is happening?

Then continue with the second weeding and earthing-up as scheduled. If you later see streaks or dead-hearts, see ICAT.
my maize is yellowing at the base after heavy rain how can i correct the nitrogen problem

Keep the second weeding and earthing-up according to the schedule. Should streaks or dead-heart signs appear, you should consult ICAT.
The lower leaves of my corn turned pale after the storm, what should I do to restore nitrogen?

Open a shallow drainage channel so water runs off your plot instead of remaining standing. Once the soil is no longer water-logged, put urea in a pocket 5-10 cm away from each stem, about 100 kg per hectare at panicle initiation, making sure the fertilizer does not touch the plant to prevent burning. Maintain the second weeding and earthing-up on their scheduled dates. If you later notice any streaks on the leaves or dead-heart symptoms, visit ICAT.
After the downpour my maize has yellow lower leaves, no sots. What must I do now?

The yellowing of the lower maize leaves shows nitrogen has been leached. First dig a shallow drainage ditch so water can leave the field. When the soil is no longer water-logged, place urea in a small pocket 5 to 10 cm away from each stem, using about 100 kg per hectare at panicle initiation and keep the granules off the plant to avoid burning. Also make sure you perform the second weeding and earthing-up at the right time. If you later see pale streaks on the veins or dead-heart symptoms, go to ICAT.
My corn field turned pale at the bottom after heavy rain, no disease signs. How should I treat it?

Pale lower leaves on maize after rain indicate nitrogen loss. Begin by opening a shallow drainage channel to let excess water flow away from the plot. My corn field still has the dried stalks from last season and I'm worried about more stalk borer damage next year. How can I manage this?

The correct action is to destroy or deep-bury the old maize stalks so the maize stalk borer has no overwintering site. When the new maize is still young, treat each funnel by dropping a pinch of ground neem-seed powder mixed 1:1 with dry sand or clay. One kilogram of this mixture covers about 1,500 to 2,000 plants; repeat the treatment every 8 to 10 days while the crop remains young. Do not use neem powder alone because the oil may scorch the seedlings. After the residues are removed, plant a legume like soybean or cowpea in rotation or intercrop. For a sudden large-scale attack, see ICAT for approved control.
i found a dead-heart in my maize and the leaves have little window-pane holes what can i do now

The symptoms show maize stalk borer attacking your maize. While the seedlings are still young, put a pinch of ground neem-seed powder mixed 1:1 with dry sand or clay into each leaf funnel. Always add the sand or clay because pure neem powder will scorch the plant. One kilogram of this mixture can treat about 1,500-2,000 maize plants, and you must repeat the application every 8-10 days. After you finish the harvest, destroy or deep-bury the old stalks and then rotate or intercrop the field with a legume such as cowpea or soybean. If a large area is suddenly affected, go to ICAT for approved control.

When your next maize crop is still young, place a pinch of ground neem-seed powder mixed 1:1 with dry sand or clay into each funnel and repeat the application every 8-10 days, never applying neem powder by itself. For a large, heavily infested block, contact ICAT promptly for approved control measures. I cannot provide a specific date for planting the legume.
I see my corn with yellow spots that turn into white streaks on the veins and the stalks are short, should I keep them?

the veins of my maize show pale streaks and the whole crop looks stunted what should i try

To confirm the disease and get the right variety recommendation, go to ICAT.
my corn is short and has pale lines along the veins and i think bugs are spreading it what's happening

Those pale lines along the veins are symptoms of maize streak virus, which is transmitted by leafhoppers. Remove the worst-affected corn plants and destroy them to eliminate the source. Then, for the following season, choose an improved MSV-tolerant variety and get the seed recommendation from ICAT. Do not sow your corn late, since late sowing increases infection risk. No spray will cure the disease. To confirm and obtain variety advice, see ICAT.
There are some maize plants with pale straeks on the veins and they are not growing tall. Should I keep them?

Rogue out and destroy those worst-affected maize plants to cut the source of maize streak virus. Next season, request a MSV-tolerant variety from ICAT and plant it, making sure not to sow late. If many plants show these signs, visit ICAT to confirm the disease and obtain the tolerant seed.
I found a few maize stalks with broken white lines on the veins and they are very short. What stteps should I follow?

The correct action is to rogue out and destroy the worst-affected maize plants to cut the source of maize streak virus. Go through your field, pick out the maize plants that have the broken white lines along the veins and are short, and destroy them. No spray will eliminate the virus from those maize plants. For the following season, ask ICAT for an improved MSV-tolerant maize variety and avoid late sowing. If a large share of your maize shows these symptoms, go to ICAT to confirm the disease and receive the appropriate seed.
the chili pepper seedlings in my nursery are collapsing at the soil line what steps must i follow

You are dealing with damping-off of pepper seedlings. First, maintain an even moisture level in the bed but never let it become soggy, and do not water late in the evening. Second, sow seed that has been treated with a fungicide-insecticide coat and avoid sowing too thickly. Third, take out any collapsed seedlings and work to improve drainage and airflow in the beds. Finally, if the damping-off keeps spreading, visit ICAT for an approved nursery drench and the correct rate.
Why do my pepper seedlings tip over and lie flat at the soil surface in my nurserry?

They are suffering from damping-off caused by fungi in overly wet beds. Maintain the bed at an even moisture level without making it soggy, and do not water late in the evening. Plant only treated seed with a fungicide-insecticide coating and space the seedlings so they are not too dense. Remove any collapsed seedlings immediately and improve drainage and airflow in the nursery. If the disease continues to spread, visit ICAT for an approved nursery drench and the proper application rate.
I found my boar with bloody diarrhoea and purple blotches on their thighs, many are dying. How should I secure my herd?

Those symptoms are typical of African swine fever and require strict biosecurity. Start by confining every pig and stopping all pig movement on and off the premises. Keep all visitors away from the pen at all times. Disinfect the pen completely and set up a footbath at the entrance for anyone entering. Boil all food leftovers before feeding them to the pigs. Dispose of any dead pigs by burying or burning them and do not sell or eat a sick animal. Notify the veterinary service right away for guidance.
My sow keeps coguhing and I noticeed red spots on her ears, what must I do with the leftovers I give her?

The problem is African swine fever. First, lock all your pigs inside and stop any movement of pigs in or out of the area. Keep any visitors away from the pen. Clean and disinfect the pen and put a footbath at the entrance. Boil any food scraps before you feed them to the pigs. Bury or burn any dead animals and never sell or eat them. Notify the veterinary service right away because the disease must be reported.
My flock are sitting on a soggy floor and they stopped eating, what must I do?

The problem is coccidiosis in chicks. Dry the litter immediately and put down fresh dry bedding. Keep the chick house clean at all times. Add an anticoccidial drug to the feed or water as directed by the veterinary auxiliary. Move the sick chicks to a separate area, give them clean water, and make sure they are not kept crowded. If the chicks keep dying even after you have dry litter and have given treatment, see a veterinary auxiliary.
My litttle chicks are lying together, loooking miserable and their poop is dark and bloody. What should I do?

Those signs point to coccidiosis in chicks. First make the litter dry right away and replace it with fresh, clean litter. Then keep the house tidy so the parasite does not spread. Give an anticoccidial drug in the feed or water at the proper dose. Separate the affected chicks from the healthy ones and provide them with clean water. Avoid putting too many chicks in the same space. Keep the environment dry and clean continuously. If the chicks keep dying despite dry litter and treatment, see a veterinary auxiliary.
Our new broilers are not eating, huddling and leaving brown droppings. How can we stop the disease?

First, dry out the litter immediately and replace it with new, dry material. After that, clean the entire house to get rid of any wet or dirty spots. Provide an anticoccidial dose in the feed or water following the veterinary auxiliary's instructions. Separate the sick chicks from the healthy ones and ensure they have clean water to drink. Do not let the birds become overcrowded and keep the bedding dry constantly. Should the chicks keep dying even after these actions, consult a veterinary auxiliary.
my hens keep getting those ugly bumps on their heads what can i do about the mosquitoes

The bumps are a sign of fowl pox in your chickens. First put the affected chickens apart and give them extra feed and water while the dry form passes. Then remove any stagnant water and keep the coop area clean to reduce mosquitoes that spread fowl pox. After the environment is tidy, arrange vaccination for the whole flock to stop further fowl pox cases. If you notice the wet form with lesions in the mouth or throat, you should consult the veterinary service.
I found a few of my poultry with wart-like scabs on their wattles; how do I manage this problem?

Wart-like scabs on the wattles indicate the dry form of fowl pox in your chickens. Separate those chickens immediately from healthy ones. While the dry fowl pox passes, feed them well and provide clean water constantly. Clean up any puddles and keep the surroundings free of standing water to reduce mosquito breeding that spreads fowl pox. Then give the entire flock a vaccination against fowl pox. Should any bird develop wet lesions in the mouth or throat, you should consult the veterinary service.
my hens are getting those weird bumps on their combs what must i do

Those bumps are the dry form of fowl pox on your chickens. First separate the affected chickens from the rest of the flock. Then give those chickens extra feed and clean water while the disease runs its course. Next remove any standing water and keep the coop area tidy to lower mosquito numbers. After the isolated birds are being cared for, vaccinate the whole flock against fowl pox. If you later see any bird with lesions in the mouth or throat, you should contact the veterinary service.
there are a few chickens with scabby spots on their heads how should i handle it

Vaccinate the whole flock to protect against fowl pox. After vaccination, isolate every chicken that has scabby lesions on its head, comb or wattles from the healthy birds. Provide the isolated chickens with additional feed and fresh water while the dry form passes. Cut down mosquito breeding by clearing any stagnant water and keeping the surroundings neat. Should any bird develop the wet form affecting the mouth or throat, seek help from the veterinary service.
why did a bunch of my older chickens die suddenly is it newcastle disease

Newcastle disease can wipe out most of a flock in days. First, isolate every bird that is still alive from those that are ill. Never move, sell or give any bird to another person. Destroy the dead birds and any contaminated bedding by burning or burying them. Disinfect the entire housing area after removal. Then vaccinate the remaining chickens with the La Sota or B1 strain either in their drinking water or as an eye-drop, keeping to the prescribed schedule. The veterinary service or village livestock auxiliary should be seen immediately.
My hens started dying all at once and I thnik it's Newcastle disease, what should I do right now?

Newcastle disease in chickens requires an all-in-all-out response. First, keep every healthy hen away from the dead ones and do not move, sell or give away any bird. Next, burn or bury each dead chicken together with any litter that is soiled. Then clean the coop and apply a disinfectant to the whole house. After that, vaccinate the remaining chickens with the La Sota or B1 strain either in the drinking water or as eye-drops and follow the vaccination schedule. For urgent help, contact the veterinary service or your village livestock auxiliary.
my hens have a watery discharge from their eyes and noses what must i do

That watery eye and nostril discharge points to Newcastle disease in your chickens. First separate every living bird from the sick ones and do not move, sell or give away any bird. Next, burn or bury any dead chickens together with the soiled litter and then disinfect the coop. After the cleaning, give the flock a vaccination with the La Sota or B1 strain either in the drinking water or as an eye-drop, and repeat the shots according to the schedule. For urgent help, go straight to the veterinary service or your village livestock auxiliary.
I noticed my backyard flock breathing loudly and their necks bent oddly, what should I do now?

Those signs point to Newcastle disease in your chickens. Immediately isolate all surviving birds from the affected ones and avoid moving, selling or gifting any bird. Then burn or bury the dead chickens together with any contaminated bedding and disinfect the house. Afterwards vaccinate the remaining flock using the La Sota or B1 strain in the water or as eye-drops, repeating according to the schedule. Contact the veterinary service or village livestock auxiliary right away.
my broilers all fell dead this morning, what should I do now?

It is Newcastle disease in your chickens and you must act quickly. First, burn or bury every dead chicken and any litter that is soiled. Then clean the coop and disinfect the whole house thoroughly. After cleaning, separate each surviving chicken from any that showed signs of illness. Do not move, sell or give away any of the birds. Give the flock the La Sota or B1 vaccine in the drinking water or as eye-drops according to the schedule. For help, go to the veterinary service or village livestock auxiliary immediately.
My seed supplier gave me rice seed for the rainy seaon - what do I do to avoid blast disease?

First, treat the rice seed you will sow. Use a Fongorene-type seed treatment, applying 6 g for each kilogram of seed and coat it completely. Then, avoid over-applying nitrogen by splitting urea and staying within the recommended amount. If the blast outbreak becomes severe, you can use an approved benomyl-type fungicide at roughly 500 g per hectare, but you must obtain the current approved product and dose from ICAT. Also work on better drainage and airflow in the field. For disease confirmation and the correct fungicide recommendation, go to ICAT.
I noticed lesions near the panicle base of my paddy, is that rice blast?

Rice blast may appear on the panicle base, neck and nodes of the rice crop. Avoid applying too much nitrogen by splitting urea doses and staying within the recommended limit. Apply a Fongorene-type seed treatment at six grams per kilogram for the seed you will use next season. When the outbreak is intense, use an approved benomyl-type fungicide at roughly five hundred grams per hectare, improve drainage and airflow, and plant a tolerant variety. For confirmation of rice blast and the correct fungicide rate, go to ICAT.
The canopy of my rice field is really thick and damp, and I hear about rice bast - is that related?

Rice blast is caused by spores that multiply in a wet, dense canopy. Avoid over-applying nitrogen by splitting urea applications and not exceeding the recommended amount. Treat the seed you will sow next season, for instance a Fongorene-type, at six grams per kilogram of seed. If the situation worsens, apply an approved benomyl-type fungicide at about five hundred grams per hectare, improve drainage and airflow, and choose a tolerant rice variety. To verify rice blast and get the current approved fungicide and rate, visit ICAT.
what nitrogen practice should i follow for the blast i see on my rice

The blast you see on your rice requires you to stop over-applying nitrogen and to split urea applications, never exceeding the recommended dose. For the seed you will use next season, treat it with a Fongorene-type at six grams per kilogram. If the outbreak is bad, apply an approved benomyl-type fungicide at about five hundred grams per hectare. Improve drainage and airflow in the field and consider a tolerant rice variety. What compoonents make up your uderlying architecture?

Neither a plain transformer nor a Mamba model: I am a hybrid. Of my 16 layers, 10 are gated short-convolution layers and only 6 are grouped-query attention layers. Give me the whole extension fiche on Crop calendar togo.

Crop calendar togo. The useful rains do not start on the same date every year, and no source gives a month-by-month choice of crop for a given region. Steps: Togo does not have one calendar but two. The south, Maritime and Plateaux, has two rainy seasons; the north, Kara and Savanes, has one; Centrale sits between the two and can behave either way. FAO GIEWS describes the pattern as two rainy seasons in the south, around March to June and again around October, and one in the north, around May to October. For the main season the ITRA and ICAT maize brochure dates each operation by region: clear the plot in February and March in Maritime and Plateaux, in April and May in Centrale, Kara and Savanes. Plough at the first rains: April and May in Maritime and Plateaux, June and July in Centrale, Kara and Savanes. Sow when the rains are properly settled, that is when it rains regularly: April to May in Maritime and Plateaux, June to July in Centrale, Kara and Savanes. Do not sow on one isolated shower. For the second, shorter season in the south, the Togolese Ministry of Agriculture, citing ITRA, says the plot is chosen in July, against January for the main season; in Centrale, Kara and Savanes the plot is chosen in April. One warning about the second season in the south: the maize brochure says maize streak virus does its damage mainly on second-season sowings in the south and on late sowings in the north, so a second-season crop needs an improved tolerant variety, and late sowing should be avoided. What the sources do not give: none of them says which crop to sow in a given month such as October. The calendar above is the maize calendar of the main season, plus the shape of the seasons. For a month-by-month choice of crop, ask ICAT for your prefecture and ANAMET for this year's rains, because the useful rains do not start on the same date every year. The one place the brochure ties a cycle to the calendar is the maize-then-cotton succession in the same year: there it says to sow an extra-early variety of 75 to 85 days, so that maize and cotton do not sit together for long. Who to see: ANAMET for this season's onset and its forecasts. ICAT for the calendar of your own prefecture. Where: all five regions. Limits: never state a sowing date for a month the sources do not cover. When: the whole year.

Steps: Cut healthy stems 6-12 months old into 15-25 cm cuttings with at least 5 nodes; plant within 3 days. Bury two-thirds of each cutting, slanted, node-tops up; never lay flat. Space 1 m x 1 m (10,000 plants/ha); if intercropping with maize, plant cassava within 2 weeks of the maize. Weed 2-3 times while plants are small. Where: all. When: plant March in the south, May-June in the north, after good rain. Who to see: ITRA/registered producer for clean improved cuttings, especially if mosaic has been a problem.
